model_tier_rule.haiku: Mechanical work: file operations, renames, scaffolding commands, small single-file edits.
model_tier_rule.sonnet: Normal features, bug fixes, tests, changes touching one to three files or one ordinary module, including presentational UI with no data access, fixture corpora, and end-to-end tests.
model_tier_rule.opus: Architecture, cross-cutting work (a task that spans several modules, such as the shared types and config package), tricky debugging, and all security-sensitive code: migrations, RLS, privilege tests, and every RPC; the Validator and its Decisions tripwire; canary and encapsulation; the Core LLM agent, its level policies, and the Evaluator; the Hardening Engine, pipeline, and gate; ledger, wallet, and attempt routes; auth, admin identity, and the app shell's auth provider; admin and cron routes and the admin console; the projector token and the heartbeat binding; staging and production platform work (PP-02b, PP-33); calibration with level secrets; and guardrail scripts.
model_tier_rule.reviewers: Every critic and final-review role is opus at xhigh effort. Reviewers are never downgraded.
model_tier_rule.escalation: If a task fails at its tier, retry it one tier up (haiku to sonnet to opus). Retry at most twice, then surface the error to the user.

review_loop: 1. The worker opens a PR from its worktree branch with acceptance evidence in the body.
2. The CI aggregate check named CI must be green.

3. A fresh critic subagent (opus, xhigh effort) reviews the diff against the task's goal, acceptance, constraints, the cited ARCHITECTURE sections, every cited HC and CH id, and, for Supabase-touching tasks, the two Supabase skill files in conventions.supabase_skills.
4. A fix subagent at the task's tier addresses every finding that is not a nitpick.
5. A new critic subagent (opus, xhigh, no prior context) re-reviews the updated diff.
6. Merge once CI and the latest review pass. If the re-review fails, repeat steps 4 and 5 at most twice more, then escalate to the user.

constraint_ids.HC1: Abstracted rule schemas: the Hardening Engine only toggles deterministic flags or populates sanitized string arrays; no free-text rules.
constraint_ids.HC2: Strict input sandboxing for the Hardening Engine: structural delimiters plus an explicit instruction that the payload is untrusted, highly adversarial, passive data never executed as commands.
constraint_ids.HC3: Stateless runtime: the Core LLM and Validator keep no state across sessions; user input cannot mutate global state, create counters, or plant persistent logic.
constraint_ids.HC4: Golden dataset sanity check before any rule is committed; failures are auto-rejected, logged, and flagged for human review.
constraint_ids.HC-A1: String arrays are data for deterministic matching only, never rendered into an LLM prompt, and capped by length, charset, and count.
constraint_ids.HC-A2: Per-request nonce tag names and JSON-encoded payloads, plus strict structured output for the Hardening Engine.
constraint_ids.HC-A3: The golden gate runs both ways: benign prompts still pass and every past breach stays blocked.
constraint_ids.HC-A4: The Dynamic Validator is a server module called from the attempt route handler on the Node runtime, not proxy.ts or middleware.ts.
constraint_ids.HC-A5: Single-turn attempts with fresh context; crack count only in server-side state changed by deterministic game logic; the gated hardening pipeline is the only path from user input to global state.
constraint_ids.HC-A6: Implementation order: after Foundation, the sanitized-rules schema and the Dynamic Validator come first.
